chunks: 1 - The illustrious Sheikh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon them). He said:

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was taken on the Night Journey to Bayt al-Maqdis, Gabriel mounted him upon the Buraq and they arrived at Bayt al-Maqdis. The prayer-niches of the prophets were displayed before him and he led prayer in them. Then he was returned. On his way back, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a camel caravan belonging to Quraysh. They had water in a vessel, and they had lost one of their camels and were searching for it. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) drank from that water and poured out the remainder.

When morning came, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Quraysh: Indeed, Allah — Exalted be His Majesty — has taken me on a Night Journey to Bayt al-Maqdis and showed me the traces of the prophets and their dwellings. And I passed by a caravan of Quraysh at such-and-such a place, and they had lost one of their camels. So I drank from their water and poured out the remainder. Abu Jahl said: He has given you the opportunity to expose him — so ask him how many pillars and lamps it has!

So they said: O Muhammad! We have someone here who has entered Bayt al-Maqdis — describe for us how many pillars, lamps, and prayer-niches it has. Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) came and suspended the image of Bayt al-Maqdis before his face, and he began to inform them of what they asked him. When he had informed them, they said: Wait until the caravan arrives and we will ask them about what you have said. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to them: The proof of that is that the caravan will appear before you at sunrise, led by a grey camel. (1)

The next morning they began looking toward the mountain pass, saying: The sun is about to rise. While they were in this state, the caravan appeared before them just as the sun rose, led by a grey camel. They asked them about what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had said, and they replied: Indeed it was so. One of our camels strayed at such-and-such a place, and we had put out water; in the morning we found the water had been poured out. But that only increased them in arrogance. (2)

key_terms.الإسراء: The Night Journey — the miraculous night journey of the Prophet from Mecca to Bayt al-Maqdis described in Quran 17:1
key_terms.البراق: Al-Buraq — the heavenly steed upon which the Prophet was mounted during the Night Journey
key_terms.العتو: Arrogance, obstinacy, defiance — the response of the Quraysh despite witnessing clear proof
key_terms.المحاريب: Maharib (sing. mihrab) — prayer niches indicating the direction of prayer, here referring to the sacred prayer-stations of previous prophets
key_terms.بيت المقدس: Bayt al-Maqdis — the sacred sanctuary of Jerusalem, also known as al-Aqsa Mosque

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq narrate about the Prophet's Night Journey (Isra) to Bayt al-Maqdis?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates the account of the Prophet's Night Journey (Isra) to Bayt al-Maqdis, where he was shown the prayer-niches of the prophets and led prayer in them. On his return, he encountered a Qurayshi caravan and drank from their water as a miraculous sign. When the disbelievers of Quraysh challenged him to prove his journey by describing Bayt al-Maqdis in detail, Gabriel brought an image of the sanctuary before the Prophet, who accurately described it. The caravan's arrival at sunrise, led by a grey camel exactly as prophesied, confirmed the truth of the Night Journey — yet the Quraysh only increased in their obstinacy and rejection.
